title: Preparation of LB Medium and Agar Plates
purpose: To prepare sterile LB liquid medium and LB agar plates (with or without antibiotic) for routine culture of E. coli and plasmid selection.
principle: LB supplies peptides and amino acids (tryptone), vitamins and trace nutrients (yeast extract) and NaCl for osmotic balance. Autoclaving sterilises the medium and agar solidifies it. Heat-labile antibiotics are added only after the medium has cooled to about 50 °C [1][3].

materials.detail: 5 g/L for LB Lennox (Miller uses 10 g/L) [2][3]
About 6.7 (NaOH) in one recipe [3]; many labs aim for 7.0
100 mg/mL in water; 0.5 mL per liter gives 50 µg/mL [1]

equipment: Bunsen burner or laminar flow hood

steps.text: Dissolve 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract and 5 g NaCl in about 800 mL water; stir until clear [3].
Adjust pH (about 6.7–7.0) with NaOH and bring to 1 L [3].
For plates, add 15 g agar per liter before autoclaving [1][3].
Autoclave at 121 °C, 15 psi, liquid cycle; loosen caps first [2][3].
Liquid LB: cool to about 50 °C or room temperature and add antibiotic only after cooling [1][3].
Agar: cool in a 50 °C water bath, swirling gently to avoid bubbles [1][2].
At about 50 °C add antibiotic (0.5 mL of 100 mg/mL ampicillin per liter for 50 µg/mL) and mix by swirling [1].
Pour 20–25 mL per 10 cm dish in a clean hood or near a flame [2].
Flame the surface briefly to pop bubbles; let plates solidify at room temperature [2].
Dry plates with lids ajar in a hood or overnight at room temperature.
Label with medium, antibiotic and date. Invert and store at 4 °C; plain plates keep for months (up to 3 months in one recipe) [2].

results: Clear, pale-yellow broth and firm, smooth, bubble-free plates.
One plate incubated overnight at 37 °C shows no growth (sterile).
Antibiotic plates select resistant transformants; plain plates support dense E. coli lawns.
controls: Incubate one plate per batch overnight at 37 °C as a sterility check
Streak a known sensitive strain on antibiotic plates
Label every batch with date and antibiotic

troubleshooting.cause: Added to hot agar or old stock
Poor sterile technique or short autoclave
troubleshooting.fix: Autoclave 15 min at 121 °C; pour near flame; discard plates [2]

troubleshooting.cause: Too little agar or short drying
troubleshooting.fix: Use 15 g/L agar; dry before storage [1][2]

safety: Hot media and autoclave steam cause burns: use heat-resistant gloves and loosen caps before autoclaving.
Agar can boil over when re-melted: heat in short bursts.
Handle antibiotic powders in a hood and dispose of used plates as biohazard waste.
